title: Notable new physics papers — arXiv announcement batch of 26 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from reported results, breadth, reusable data or methods, and other checkable signals. The selected new preprints currently have zero Semantic Scholar citation and influential-citation totals, so popularity evidence is sparse.

sections.title: Entangled logical qubits on a superconducting quantum processor
sections.abstract: We demonstrate high-fidelity logical qubit operations using ibm_phoenix, a square-lattice array of 120 coupled superconducting qubits that are capable of fast reset. Using strategies to exclude underperforming components together with noise informed decoding, we routinely produce surface codes at distance-3 and distance-5 with logical error per round below 1%. We demonstrate entanglement between two logical qubits, where logical Bell-state fidelities above 93% are observed for entanglement created via lattice surgery. With three logical qubits and lattice surgery, we perform logical teleportation of a range of states and gates, observing fidelities in the range 78% - 93%. Using reset to reduce qubit leakage, we show that repeated rounds of stabilizer measurements continue to exhibit improvements in a stability experiment up to approximately 2×10^-7 over 170 measurement rounds.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report lattice-surgery Bell-state fidelities above 93% and teleportation fidelities of 78–93% on ibm_phoenix; a fast-reset stability experiment reaches an error probability near 2×10^-7 after 170 rounds.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; IBM ibm_phoenix, a 120-coupled-qubit superconducting processor, with surface-code experiments and lattice surgery
sections.unique_caveat: The work depends on excluding underperforming qubits and noise-informed decoding. Bell-state fidelity bounds use XX and ZZ measurements rather than full YY tomography, and selected results use post-selection.
sections.ranking_evidence: A substantial hardware demonstration combines error-corrected logical entanglement, state/gate teleportation, and a long stability run, with quantitative performance reported in the paper's results and appendices.

sections.title: Three subpopulations of binary black holes in mass, spin magnitudes and tilts following GWTC-5
sections.abstract: The mass and spin distributions of merging binary black holes offer clues to their formation pathways, which remain uncertain. In this work, we model the population of binary black holes using generic subpopulations with distinct mass-ratio, spin-magnitude, and spin-tilt distributions, whose relative contributions vary with primary mass. Using the 259 binary black holes in the fifth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA catalog (GWTC-5), we resolve three subpopulations with low, medium, and high spins. The low-spin population dominates for primary masses near 35 solar masses, contributes roughly half of the binaries for primary masses of 10 solar masses, and favors nearly equal mass ratios overall; its spins are consistent with both black holes having negligible spin, with a log Bayes factor of 6.1 (+0.2/-0.3) in favor of vanishing spins. The medium-spin population accounts for the other half of the population around primary masses of 10 solar masses and favors spin magnitudes around 0.2 for both components, preferentially aligned orientations, and comparable mass ratios. The high-spin population dominates above primary masses of 60 solar masses and also contributes at lower masses around 20 solar masses; it favors a rapidly spinning primary around 0.7, a broad range of secondary spins, widely distributed spin orientations, and a broad mass-ratio distribution. Allowing for a fourth subpopulation yields no distinct additional mass-ratio or spin distribution, as it becomes degenerate with existing features. To resolve highly concentrated features in spin, we control the variance of standard Monte Carlo likelihood estimators using truncated Gaussian mixture models. Taken together, our results add to a growing body of evidence for substructure in the population of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA black holes, providing further clues to uncover their formation histories.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer three black-hole binary subpopulations and find that a fourth does not yield a distinct additional mass-ratio or spin distribution under their model.
sections.evidence_type: observational; hierarchical Bayesian population inference using the 259 binary black holes in the fifth LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA catalog (GWTC-5)
sections.unique_caveat: The population structure is model-dependent; inferred components overlap, and a fourth component becomes degenerate with existing features. These are population inferences, not direct identifications of individual formation channels.
sections.ranking_evidence: The authors analyze a large gravitational-wave catalog and report a quantified population split, including a Bayes factor of about 10^6 in favor of negligible spins for the low-spin component; the paper explicitly tests whether a fourth component is distinguishable.

sections.title: Equation of state of hot and dense QCD using the complex Langevin equation
sections.abstract: We present continuum-extrapolated lattice results for the QCD equation of state at high temperatures and unprecedentedly large baryon chemical potentials. These results were obtained by performing the first complex Langevin simulations at the physical value of the pion mass. We work in a strangeness-neutral, charm-neutral, and isospin-symmetric setup and show results for the baryon density, pressure, and trace anomaly as a function of baryon chemical potential and temperature, respectively.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report continuum-extrapolated thermodynamic observables for strangeness-neutral, charm-neutral, isospin-symmetric QCD as functions of temperature and baryon chemical potential.
sections.evidence_type: computational; lattice simulations with complex Langevin dynamics and continuum extrapolation
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that singularities in the complex Langevin drift currently restrict their approach to high temperatures, preventing reliable extension to lower-temperature regions.
sections.ranking_evidence: The work spans lattice and theoretical high-energy physics and reports a physical-pion-mass calculation in a regime where the usual lattice sign problem obstructs standard importance sampling; the approach and its practical limits are detailed in the full text.

sections.title: Nano-ARPES observation of a flat band at the \bar{M} point in 2.4° twisted bilayer graphene
sections.abstract: The emergence of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at the so-called magic angle reveals a range of intriguing phases, such as superconductivity and Mott insulating states, resulting from electrons entering a correlated state. This establishes twisted bilayer graphene as an excellent platform for exploring correlation effects in many-body phases and across various twist angles. However, in most cases, the twist angle is not an easy parameter to control because it exhibits structural instabilities such as relaxation and reconstruction that reduce the correlation effects. Here, we report the unexpected appearance of a flat band at the M point far from the Fermi level in a 2.4° twisted bilayer graphene, directly visualized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. Our work is the first observation of flat bands away from the K point in twisted bilayer graphene and highlights the need to probe the entire Brillouin zone to fully capture electronic states in twisted structures.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report direct angle-resolved photoemission visualization of a flat band at M in a 2.4° twisted-bilayer sample and argue that the full Brillouin zone should be probed.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; nano-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) on twisted bilayer graphene
sections.unique_caveat: The reported observation is for a particular twist-angle sample; structural relaxation and reconstruction can affect twist-angle control and the resulting electronic structure.
sections.ranking_evidence: This is a direct spectroscopic observation of an electronic feature outside the usual K-point focus, with relevance to both mesoscale physics and materials science.
sections.comment: Main text (11 pages, 4 figures) and supplementary material (3 pages, 3 figures)

sections.title: Heavy Sterile Fermions from the Atmosphere: LZ Limits on Neutrino Up-Scattering
sections.abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has recently reported data extending to nuclear-recoil energies of about 270 keV, including a single event at 248 keV in a nearly background-free region, for an exposure of 2.84 tonne-years. We examine this dataset through neutrino up-scattering to a heavy sterile fermion induced by atmospheric neutrinos, mediated by vector, axial-vector, scalar and dipole interactions. Our main result is a set of constraints: using the part of the LZ data where no excess is observed, we obtain new bounds on all four scenarios that probe regions of parameter space not tested before, and show that dark matter detectors can provide competitive limits on neutrino up-scattering for sterile fermion masses above approximately 50 MeV. We also test whether the 248 keV event can be explained in this way while remaining consistent with the absence of events at lower recoil energies. For the scalar, vector and axial mediators this requires couplings at the edge of perturbativity, while the dipole does not provide a good fit, so we conclude that up-scattering is not a compelling explanation of the event.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report new bounds for all four interaction scenarios, with competitive sensitivity above sterile-fermion masses of roughly 50 MeV, and conclude that the 248 keV event is not compellingly explained by the tested up-scattering models.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; phenomenological reanalysis of LUX-ZEPLIN nuclear-recoil data, including the reported 248 keV event
sections.unique_caveat: The bounds depend on the assumed mediator and coupling structure; for several interactions, fitting the event requires couplings near the edge of perturbativity, while the dipole case fits poorly.
sections.ranking_evidence: The analysis connects a dark-matter detector dataset with particle-phenomenology models across experiment and theory, deriving constraints for four mediator cases from a 2.84 tonne-year LZ exposure.

sections.title: Electron Wavefronts Capture Nanoscale Movies of Hypersound at Surfaces
sections.abstract: Acoustic waves transport mechanical energy and elastic strain through solids, with material composition and shape governing their propagation. In the gigahertz hypersound regime, acoustic wavelengths reach tens to hundreds of nanometres, comparable to nanoscale device dimensions. Harnessing these waves underpins high-frequency signal processing, sensing, electromagnetic coupling and quantum control. Acoustic metrology probes elastic modes and internal interfaces. Yet directly imaging how nanoscale acoustic waves interact with local structure remains challenging, requiring picometre displacement sensitivity combined with high spatiotemporal resolution. Here we demonstrate full-field imaging of laser-induced hypersound at surfaces using reflected electron wavefronts. We introduce ultrafast low-energy electron microscopy (ULEEM), exploiting the intrinsic surface sensitivity of few-electronvolt electrons. Coherent electron pulses down to femtosecond durations reflect from the topmost atomic layers, imprinting the evolving surface profile onto their wavefronts. Defocus converts phase variations into image contrast. In a thin van der Waals material, we image the thermoelastic generation and propagation of picometre-amplitude acoustic waves. Measured dispersion relations, interpreted through elastodynamic modelling, distinguish substrate-supported and locally detached regions, revealing how interfacial contact shapes propagation. Delayed wave emission reveals scattering at buried mechanical defects. Our results establish electron-wavefront imaging of nanoscale surface dynamics, enabling the exploration of ultrafast energy transport, structural transformations and coupled mechanical, electronic and magnetic phenomena.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report imaging thermoelastic hypersound in a thin van der Waals material and distinguishing supported from locally detached regions, with delayed emission indicating scattering at buried mechanical defects.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ultrafast low-energy electron microscopy with femtosecond electron pulses, supported by elastodynamic modeling
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstration is in a thin van der Waals material; broader performance across materials and device geometries remains to be established.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper introduces a full-field, surface-sensitive imaging method and combines measured dispersion with elastodynamic modeling; it is cross-listed across materials, instrumentation, and optics, and includes supplementary videos.
sections.comment: 22 pages including 5 pages of Supplementary Information, 5 main figures, 2 Extended Data figures, 8 supplementary videos

sections.title: The renormalization of the shell-model neutrinoless double-beta decay operator starting from effective field theory at next-to-next-to-leading order
sections.abstract: This paper is the continuation of a previous study, where shell-model calculations of the matrix elements for the neutrinoless double-beta decay were performed within a fully-consistent framework, starting from expressions of the nuclear Hamiltonian and decay operators which have been derived through chiral perturbation theory. The decays under our investigation are those involving 48Ca, 76Ge, and 82Se, as in our earlier analyses of electroweak nuclear decays with Hamiltonians and operators derived within effective field theory. In this work we focus on perturbative properties of the chiral expansion of the decay operator, namely in assessing the weight of terms beyond the leading order on the nuclear matrix elements of medium-mass candidates. To this end, we have constructed effective shell-model decay operators starting from two-body currents up to next-to-next-to-leading order and, for the first time, we introduce for nuclei of experimental interest contributions of the three-body current operators, which emerge at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order of the chiral perturbation theory. Our investigation is aimed to evaluate the theoretical uncertainties affecting the calculated nuclear matrix elements of the neutrinoless double-beta decay, by conjugating the estimate of the inaccuracy related to the finiteness of the degrees of freedom of the nuclear model and the truncation of the chiral expansion of the decay operator.
sections.claimed_result: The authors construct effective shell-model decay operators through next-to-next-to-leading order in two-body currents and introduce next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order three-body currents for the three candidate isotopes.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; shell-model calculations using chiral effective-field-theory Hamiltonians and decay operators
sections.unique_caveat: The matrix elements retain uncertainties from finite nuclear-model spaces and truncation of the chiral expansion; quantifying those uncertainties is the stated purpose, not a resolved experimental decay measurement.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper is cross-listed in four nuclear and high-energy physics areas and directly targets theoretical uncertainty in nuclear matrix elements relevant to experimental searches.
sections.comment: 15 pages, 3 figures, 7 tables, submitted to Physical Review C

sections.title: Introducing the GION Lightcone Simulation Suite for Multi-Wavelength Large-Scale Structure Cosmology
sections.abstract: We present the GION (Ginkaku Lightcone Multi-wavelength Simulation Project) simulation suite: 10 full-sky high-resolution cosmological lightcone simulations and their associated products for multi-wavelength large-scale structure cosmology. We use the TreePM N-body code GINKAKU, which is highly optimized in the massively parallel environment, and integrate the on-the-fly lightcone construction technique. Each lightcone simulation is run with 6144^3 particles in a volume of (1.5 h^-1 Gpc)^3, which corresponds to a particle mass of 1.28×10^9 h^-1 solar masses, and extends to redshift 5. The fine mass resolution and the depth of the lightcone simulations allow us to resolve dark matter halos down to 10^11 h^-1 solar masses in the high-redshift Universe, which is crucial for applications to Stage-IV cosmological surveys. The fundamental statistics of the simulations, including the matter power spectrum, halo power spectrum, and halo mass function, are validated against theoretical predictions. We also generate various large-scale structure observables from the lightcone outputs: dark matter halo catalogs, mock galaxy samples, weak-lensing convergence maps, and thermal and kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ and kSZ) maps. The angular power spectra of these observables, including the cross-correlation between weak lensing and the tSZ effect, are in good agreement with theoretical predictions, demonstrating that the suite provides mutually consistent multi-wavelength observables on the same lightcone. The GION simulation suite will be publicly available and can be used for various cosmological analyses to address observational systematic effects and validate theoretical models.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that the suite's matter/halo statistics and multi-wavelength angular power spectra agree with theoretical predictions, including weak-lensing/tSZ cross-correlations.
sections.evidence_type: computational; ten full-sky, high-resolution GINKAKU N-body lightcone simulations extending to redshift 5, with public data at the GION_Data_Release repository
sections.unique_caveat: Validation is against theoretical predictions and internal cross-statistics, not a direct validation against survey observations; use in survey analyses still requires modeling observational systematics.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper describes a reusable 10-lightcone simulation suite and a public data release, including halo catalogs, mock galaxies, weak-lensing maps, and thermal/kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich maps.
sections.comment: 40 pages, 16 figures, submitted to PRD, data are available at https://github.com/GION-simulations/GION_Data_Release
